# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (§3 R1–R11 as candidates); ranking and track confirmed in your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). | uv workspace with four member packages (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes over a chosen range, downloaded and kept as the baseline (R1) | A | 1 | Bytes per quarter measured by Stage 1; full range = that × quarters chosen (no start year assumed, §4.8). Request count is small at 3 req/s (§4.8). |
| O2 | Daily filing indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, with catch-up after missed runs (R2) | A | 2 | About one listing plus one file per business day; not material |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet built from the downloaded indexes (R3) | A | 3 | Elapsed time and peak memory per quarter measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The ingestion running on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor (R4) | A | 4 | Azure dollars: no estimate until resource sizes are chosen (§4.8 leaves them to the plan); measured by Stage 7's smoke run |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs sharing one downloader, parser and publisher (R5) | A | 5 | not material |
| O6 | Reprocessing from stored original bytes after a parser change, with no new download (R6) | A | 6 | Raw storage equals O1 plus O2 volume; no SEC traffic |
| O7 | Periodic reconciliation of the quarterly baseline against later SEC corrections (R7) | A | 7 | Re-reads every supported quarter weekly (§4.8), so O1's full-range bytes once a week |
| O8 | All SEC traffic going through one downloader under one request budget (R8) | A | 8 | not material |
| O9 | Readers getting each quarter's current dataset through one versioned active pointer (R9) | A | 9 | not material |
| O10 | Closed-quarter withdrawals applied only after explicit approval bound to the source hash (R10) | A | 10 | Your partner's time: one review per gated candidate; frequency unknown until Stage 6 runs on real data |
| O11 | Stated starting defaults for schedules, retries and rate, validated before any request (R11) | A | 11 | not material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Open questions

1. Package layout. Spec §4.9 places all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repo instead scaffolds four packages: `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest` and `sec-edgar-ingest`. The root script `sec-edgar = "sec_edgar:main"` also names a module that does not exist. Stage 1's brainstorming settles this.
2. Acceptance. The ADR and the spec are both PROPOSED, and R4 is "subject to ADR acceptance" (§3). Stages 1–6 run locally and do not depend on that acceptance. Stage 7 consumes it.

## Stages

Order follows dependencies and information order, and departs from the confirmed ranking. Stage 1 delivers O1 and O3 on one real quarter, which gives the cheap cost measurement. O8 and O11 come next because every later stage makes SEC requests. O2 (rank 2) waits for the manifest and publication contracts, which daily ingestion writes into. O4 (rank 4) comes last but one: it re-hosts finished contracts and needs the ADR accepted.

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter, end to end, locally
      Objective: Download one archived quarterly master index and publish it as canonical Parquet on local disk.
      Outcomes: O1 (one quarter), O3 (one quarter)
      Consumes: an SEC identity for `sec.user_agent` (§4.8); one archived quarter chosen by your partner; Open question 1
      Produces: a downloader and parser yielding rows under the §4.5 row contract (`sec-index-v1`), with raw bytes and SHA-256 kept; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the quarter's original bytes are stored with their SHA-256 and byte count. O3 — a Parquet file whose rows meet every §4.5 field contract, with its row count reported. Measured cost of the real run: bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and observed request rate, recorded in the findings file.
      Leaves out: retry policy and typed configuration (Stage 2); source manifest, checkpoints and replay (Stage 3); golden fixtures over the range (Stage 3); versioned generations and active pointer (Stage 4); daily sources (Stage 5); reconciliation (Stage 6); Azure platform, cross-host lease, monitoring and alerts (Stage 7); scheduling and runbooks (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Shared downloader, request budget and configuration
      Objective: Route all SEC access through one throttled, retrying downloader and validate configuration before any request.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader
      Produces: retry policy and typed configuration per §4.3, §4.8 and §5 (Configuration, Throttled/transient, Access blocked, Invalid source); quarantine of invalid bodies
      Exit: O8 — CI shows concurrent callers in one process sharing the budget, with retries counted against it (§6 Access, excluding lease takeover). O11 — every §5 Configuration case is refused before any external I/O, in CI.
      Leaves out: cross-host lease (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Source manifest, worksets, backfill and replay
      Objective: Backfill a configured quarter range through checkpointed discover/collect/transform commands, with replay from raw bytes.
      Outcomes: O1 (range), O5, O6
      Consumes: Stage 2's retry policy and typed configuration; `backfill.start_quarter` and `backfill.end_quarter` chosen by your partner (§7 step 1)
      Produces: source manifest, worksets, checkpoints and replay per §4.1, §4.2 (Backfill), §4.3 and §4.5 (Source manifest), on a local storage backend; golden fixtures over the range (§4.6)
      Exit: O1 — a real backfill over a small range reports complete, pending and failed units separately. O5 — backfill runs through the shared discover, collect and transform commands. O6 — a replay with SEC access disabled yields identical logical rows, and an interrupted run resumes without losing completed units (§6 Replay).
      Leaves out: versioned generations and active pointer (Stage 4); Azure platform (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Versioned generations and active pointer
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3's source manifest and storage backend
      Produces: versioned generations and active pointer per §4.5 (paths, Quarter publication) and §4.6 (Publish); changes.parquet per generation; a `publish` command
      Exit: O9 — the §6 Publication crash-injection and competing-publisher tests pass, and readers resolve only the pointer's manifest file list.
      Leaves out: Azure platform, including Table Storage conditional writes (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from the handoff date, including outage catch-up and baseline overlap.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 3's source manifest; Stage 4's versioned generations and active pointer; `daily.start_date` chosen by your partner
      Produces: daily discovery and open-quarter precedence per §4.2 (Daily ingestion) and §4.4 (Open quarter)
      Exit: O2 — the §6 Discovery and coverage cases pass in CI, and a real catch-up over a recent span publishes the open quarter with overlap deduplicated and `no_new_sources` reported where it applies.
      Leaves out: scheduling (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Refresh quarterly sources, publish safe changes automatically and gate withdrawals behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4's versioned generations and active pointer; Stage 5's daily observations
      Produces: a reconciliation workflow and approval records per §4.2 (Reconciliation), §4.4 (Closed quarter, Changes) and §4.5 (Withdrawal approval)
      Exit: O7 — a real reconciliation over the backfilled range records additions and updates, and skips quarters whose bytes are unchanged. O10 — the §6 Reconciliation cases pass, including stale daily replay not resurrecting a withdrawn key.
      Leaves out: scheduling (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure platform
      Objective: Run the shared commands on the R4 platform in an isolated environment, with production triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4, O8 (cross-host lease)
      Consumes: the ADR and the spec accepted (Open question 2); Stages 1–6's commands and contracts
      Produces: the Azure platform per §4.1, §4.7 and §4.9, including the cross-host lease (§4.3), monitoring and alerts, and infrastructure as code
      Exit: O4 — integration tests pass on isolated Azure resources (§6 Integration, §6 Orchestration), and the bounded live smoke run and SEC-disabled replay of §7 steps 3–5 are recorded with byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest and request rate. O8 — the lease-loss and takeover tests show no overlapping request issuers.
      Leaves out: scheduling and runbooks (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill and catch-up, then enable the daily and reconciliation triggers.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 (in production)
      Consumes: Stage 7's Azure platform, monitoring and alerts
      Produces: scheduling and runbooks per §4.8 (schedules), §7 steps 6–9 and §8; a release record
      Exit: O1 — every requested baseline unit is published, or the incomplete range is recorded as approved. O2 and O7 — observed scheduled executions match their durable reports (§7 Exit).
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O11 against the accumulated system, with evidence for each verdict: the implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes and deferred_items entries (derive-roadmap §6). Each unmet outcome exits one of two ways: a new stage, which keeps the roadmap live, or a conscious deferral with a written reason.
